'''Jamie Ager''' (born November 18, 1977)<ref name="hng-birthday" /><ref name="citizen-times" /> is an American farmer, businessman, and politician who is the member-elect of the [[United States House of Representatives]] from [[North Carolina's 11th congressional district]]. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], Ager is the co-founder and chief executive of Hickory Nut Gap, a regenerative farm and locally sourced meat distributor based on his family's farm in [[Fairview, Buncombe County, North Carolina|Fairview, North Carolina]]. Ager is the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee for [[North Carolina's 11th congressional district]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in North Carolina|2026 election]].<ref name="newsline-primary" /><ref name="citizen-times" />

== Early life and education ==
Ager grew up on Hickory Nut Gap Farm in Fairview, North Carolina, in [[Buncombe County, North Carolina|Buncombe County]].<ref name="wlos-primary" /> The farm was established in 1916 by Jim and Elizabeth McClure, founders of the Farmers Federation agricultural cooperative, and passed through the Clarke family to the Agers.<ref name="provisioner" /><ref name="citizen-times-mcclure" /> His grandfather, [[James McClure Clarke]], represented North Carolina's 11th congressional district from 1983 to 1985 and from 1987 to 1991.<ref name="newsline-primary" /><ref name="citizen-times" /> His father, [[John Ager]], represented the 115th district in the [[North Carolina House of Representatives]] from 2015 to 2023, and his brother, [[Eric Ager]], has represented the 114th district since 2023.<ref name="citizen-times" /><!-- Add a source for the district numbers, e.g. the NC General Assembly member pages. -->

Ager graduated from [[A.C. Reynolds High School]] in [[Asheville, North Carolina|Asheville]] and earned degrees in environmental studies and history from [[Warren Wilson College]] in [[Swannanoa, North Carolina|Swannanoa]], with a focus on sustainable agriculture.<ref name="wlos-primary" /><ref name="provisioner" />

== Farming and business career ==
After college, Ager visited the farmer and author [[Joel Salatin]] to study pasture-based livestock production.<ref name="provisioner" /> Ager and his wife, Amy, married in 2001 and founded Hickory Nut Gap Meats, a business that direct-markets grass-fed beef and pastured poultry, sourcing meat from its own farm as well as from other local producers. The company began with a single restaurant customer in [[Asheville, North Carolina|Asheville]] and later expanded to source from a network of partner farms across the region.<ref name="provisioner" /> As of 2025, the company employed about 25 people.<ref name="announcement" /><!-- Campaign source; acceptable for uncontroversial self-description under WP:ABOUTSELF. Replace with an independent source if one is found. -->

Hickory Nut Gap Farm was badly damaged by [[Hurricane Helene]] in September 2024, which struck during the farm's harvest season, when it typically earns more than half of its annual revenue.<ref name="marketplace" /> Afterward, Ager hosted community cookouts for neighbors affected by the storm,<ref name="wsoc" /> and the farm store reopened by mid-October 2024.<ref name="marketplace" /> In March 2025, the company lost its contract to supply beef to Buncombe County schools after the [[United States Department of Agriculture]] ended the pandemic-era Local Food for Schools program, which had funded purchases from local farms.<ref name="wlos-usda" /><ref name="wsoc" />

== 2026 congressional campaign ==
Ager announced his candidacy for North Carolina's 11th congressional district on July 31, 2025, his first run for elected office.<ref name="announcement" /><ref name="citizen-times" /> In the March 3, 2026, Democratic primary, he won 64.7 percent of the vote against four opponents.<ref name="newsline-primary" /><ref name="nbc-results" /> The [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee]] added him to its "Red to Blue" program for competitive Republican-held seats.<ref name="newsline-primary" />

Ager describes himself as a "Mountain Democrat." He has said he does not accept corporate [[political action committee]] money, and he signed the centrist "Promise to America" pledge, which drew criticism from some on the party's left.<ref name="bpr-july" /> His campaign has emphasized Hurricane Helene recovery funding, cost of living, health care, immigration reform, and anti-corruption measures.<ref name="wlos-primary" /><ref name="bpr-july" /> On energy and the environment, he has said he supports the cheapest available energy sources including solar, and opposes cuts to the [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]].<ref name="mountainx-env" /> He has said he supports a short-term moratorium on new data center construction in Western North Carolina.<ref name="sace" /> He was endorsed by the [[Blue Dog Coalition|Blue Dog PAC]].<ref>https://bluedogdems.com/johnny-garcia/</ref> Between July 2025 and February 2026, Ager raised more than $940,000, outpacing incumbent Republican [[Chuck Edwards]].<ref name="citizen-times" />

Ager was originally set to face Edwards in the general election. In August 2026, Edwards withdrew from the race after the [[United States House Committee on Ethics|House Ethics Committee]] recommended he be censured over allegations of inappropriate conduct toward two female aides.<ref name="wlos-edwards" /> On August 10, 2026, the district's Republican executive committee selected state representative [[Jennifer Balkcom]] as the replacement nominee.<ref name="newsline-balkcom" /> [[Sabato's Crystal Ball]] moved the race to "Toss-up" in late July 2026,<ref name="newsline-balkcom" /> while the [[Cook Political Report]] rated it "Lean Republican" as of September 2026.<ref name="cook" /> The general election is scheduled for November 3, 2026.

== Personal life ==
Ager lives in Fairview with his wife, Amy, with whom he has three sons.<ref name="announcement" /> The couple hosts monthly barn dances at their farm.<ref name="newsline-ads" />
